paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples with a larger number of examples
model_annotation: The line chart compares the performance of two example selection strategies—ST-ES and Random—as measured by minFDE₂₀ (in units of distance) across varying numbers of in-context examples, ranging from 0 to 15. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Examples,” is linearly scaled from 0 to 15 with tick marks at regular intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled “minFDE₂₀ (←),” is linearly scaled from 0.85 to 1.05 with tick marks at regular intervals of 0.01. The ST-ES strategy is represented by a blue line with circular markers and a solid line, starting at a value of approximately 1.05 at 0 examples and decreasing to approximately 0.82 at 15 examples, with a steep initial drop followed by a gradual leveling off. The Random strategy is represented by an orange line with circular markers and a solid line, starting at approximately 1.04 at 0 examples and fluctuating slightly around a value of approximately 0.98 from 2 to 15 examples, showing minor oscillations without a clear trend.
